summary: The Orthodox Confession of Peter Mogila says every Christian should submit to and obey the Church, as Christ taught, and that the Church is fully empowered to examine and warrant the Scripture and to judge patriarchs, popes and bishops in her general councils. The questions read do not set out the relationship of Scripture and tradition or list the books of Scripture.

points.question: Who interprets Scripture?
points.answer: Every Christian must submit to the Church; in her general councils she has authority to examine and warrant the Scripture, and to inquire into the conduct of patriarchs, popes, bishops and all others.

scriptureNote: Passage the confession cites in the answer read.

document.title: The Orthodox Confession of the Catholic and Apostolic Eastern Church
document.section: Part I, Question 86 (the church and Scripture)
document.issuer: The Orthodox Church (drafted by Metropolitan Peter Mogila of Kiev; endorsed by the Eastern patriarchs)
document.date: 1640s; endorsed by the Eastern patriarchs in 1643 (from general knowledge, unchecked)
document.edition: English translation attributed to Philip Lodvel (1772), as printed in the 1898 London edition on azbyka.ru

rights.note: The confession is from the 1640s and the English translation from 1772, so only one short sentence is quoted. The web copy's own rights are not separately confirmed.

review.note: Question 86 read on 2026-11-12 in the azbyka.ru English text, with Q. 83-85 and 96 on the nature of the Church; the confession's longer treatment of Scripture, tradition and the canon was not read, so those two cells are "not stated". The confession cites the Wisdom of Solomon as Scripture elsewhere. Not yet checked by a second reviewer.
